signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Shock
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades near 114.43 as the G10 leader-to-laggard spread widens to 1.661%, marking a strong G10 bilateral theme. The move is fueled by crude oil's rally to $83.4 following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, providing structural support to CAD (1W avg +0.789%) against a weak JPY (1W avg -0.872%). While the +125bp CORRA-TONA carry advantage favors CAD, JPY data has actually outperformed (ESI +13.8), suggesting the current divergence is driven almost entirely by the commodity supply shock and energy-led inflation fears. Resistance holds near the SMA200 at 158.09 on the USD/JPY side, while CAD/JPY momentum remains tied to the duration of the maritime disruption. Trade bias: Bullish CAD/JPY; commodity supply shock overrides neutral positioning. Catalyst: Next WTI crude settlement. Risk: Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz triggers a sharp reversal in energy-linked CAD strength.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.35, holding below the SMA20/50 cluster at 161.08/161.16 but above the SMA200 at 158.09. Despite a +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage, USD/JPY options show unusual complacency with a VRP of -1.8% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.9%). BoJ holds at 1.0%. This options skew contradicts the crowded spec short in JPY (LF net -63,633), suggesting a high-conviction hedge against a carry unwind if the BoJ accelerates its tightening cycle. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options market hedging for a hawkish BoJ surprise. Catalyst: Next high-impact US data release. Risk: US 10Y yields break above 4.80%, re-asserting carry dominance over BoJ policy shifts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3505 sits above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3367–1.3420), but positioning is reaching stretched levels with COT LF net long at +39,039 (70.1% long). The options market is pricing a heavy premium for volatility, with a +5.0% VRP (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%) as traders brace for the US CPI release. Although the SOFR-SONIA carry is neutral (+0bp), the high vol premium suggests the market is paying up for protection rather than extending the current bullish trend. Retail sentiment aligns with this caution, showing a 70% short bias that has yet to be squeezed out. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; extreme vol premium and 70% long positioning suggest trend exhaustion. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: CPI miss triggers a dollar sell-off, forcing a final squeeze of the retail short toward 1.3600.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5882 remains above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5789–0.5842) following a 1M gain of +2.08%. The setup shows a sharp divergence between speculative positioning (COT LF net short -30,785, 9.7% long) and underlying fundamentals (ESI at +24.4, the strongest in G10). While NZD carry remains at a -125bp deficit vs USD, the sustained data beats and a hawkish RBNZ bias create an asymmetric squeeze risk for the crowded spec short. If incoming data continues to outperform, a move toward 0.6000 becomes the likely path for short-covering. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; asymmetric squeeze potential against crowded spec shorts. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: Sharp drop in risk appetite (VIX > 25) forces a liquidation of high-beta NZD longs.

signals.title: EUR/CHF — Retail Extreme + Put Skew
signals.text: EUR/CHF trades at 0.9360 with a +240bp carry advantage for the Euro (€STR 2.19% vs SARON -0.05%). Retail sentiment is at an extreme 86% short, frequently a precursor to a squeeze higher, yet the institutional options market is paying for protection against EUR weakness (25d RR -0.31). Speculative positioning in CHF remains net short (-12,207), and with VIX at 15.3, safe-haven demand for CHF is currently suppressed. The pair is caught between a favorable carry profile and institutional hedging for a potential ECB shift. Trade bias: Neutral/Range EUR/CHF; retail extreme short vs institutional put skew. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: Unexpected spike in geopolitical risk drives CHF safe-haven demand, validating the options skew.
